question: Assuming Gareth Evan's Generality Constraint, if I understand a proposition Fa, should I be able to understand Fx (\forall x)? Assume I understand universal quantification.

7.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: Yes, under Evans' Generality Constraint the grasp of Fa already commits one to a prior comprehension of the open sentence Fx (understood as a predicate with a free variable position), which then combines with the independently understood universal quantifier to yield Fx(∀x). The constraint rules out any understanding of a singular instance that does not already involve mastery of the corresponding predicate in open form; otherwise the thought would lack the required recombinability across different objects. This priority of the open sentence is what allows the quantifier to be applied without further conceptual innovation.
